title: The king who asked to be a step
hookLine: a king's wish list: a fish in the temple pond, a tree on the hill, a step at the shrine's door
carry: dasya: a servant's love, always facing god
tomorrow: a singer kept outside the temple. who carries him in?

lines: A FISH, A BIRD, A TREE.
A STEP AT THE SHRINE'S DOOR.
cards: A king sits down to write a wish list. He already has the throne, the palace, the army. So what does he wish for?
To be a fish in a temple pond. A bird by the water. A flowering tree on a hill.

And finally, a stone step at the door of a shrine, the kind people walk on without looking down. That king, in Sri Vaishnava tradition, is Kulasekhara, one of the Alvars, and the wish list is one of his hymns.

teach.b: The Alvars were poet-saints of Vishnu who sang in Tamil, and the tradition explains their name as people sunk deep in God. Now Kulasekhara.

Tradition remembers him as a king of the Chera country, on India's southwest coast, who loved the Lord more than his crown. His hymns are gathered as the Perumal Tirumozhi, the holy words of the king.
In one set of verses he turns toward Venkatam, the sacred hill of Vishnu, and makes his wishes.
Something small on that hill: a bird by the pond, a fish in its water, a servant who carries things for the Lord, a tree that flowers there. And then the image that stayed.
Let me lie as a step, he sings, so I can see your coral mouth. Stood on by everyone who comes, low and still, but always facing the Lord.

teach.h: LET ME LIE AS A STEP.
teach.b: The tradition says the threshold step of the shrine at Tirupati, on that hill, carries his name to this day: Kulasekharan padi, Kulasekhara's step.
The verses end with something like: let me be anything at all on that hill. Notice what the king gives up: not just wealth, but height.
Hindu bhakti has a name for this love: dasya, a servant's love, one of the forms the Narada sutras listed yesterday. The servant's place is low, but it's the one that always faces the Lord.
So the one who sets out the chairs at the puja, or stands at the back, isn't lower here. In the king's hymn, that's the clearest view.

how: In Sri Vaishnava worship, the Alvars' Tamil hymns are recited in temples and homes, and pilgrims at Tirupati are told of Kulasekhara Alvar's wish to be a step before the Lord.

games.q: you're a king with everything a king can have, singing to the Lord of Venkatam. what do you ask to become?
o: a step at the shrine's door.
games.why: Kulasekhara asks to lie as a step so he can see the Lord's coral mouth, and finally to be anything at all on that hill.

practice: Let your gaze drop to the floor a little way in front of you, the height a step would see from, and let thoughts of rank, titles, who's ahead, what you're owed, pass over you like footsteps.

Then lift your eyes just a little, toward a picture, a window or the open space ahead, and keep that one direction, the way the step keeps facing the shrine. If you pray, you can face God this way, from the threshold.
